237 hours in, and Halo Infinite still has its hooks in me. The core gameplay is razor-sharp—movement feels fluid, gunplay is classic Halo with modern polish, and when matches click, they really click. The sandbox rewards skill, positioning, and creativity in a way few shooters still manage.

Multiplayer has evolved a lot since launch, and the steady updates, new modes, and maps have kept things fresh. It’s the kind of game I boot up “for one match” and suddenly an hour disappears. Ranked can be sweaty, casual modes stay fun, and the moment-to-moment combat never gets old.

It’s not perfect, but the foundation is rock solid—and that’s why I’m still playing after hundreds of hours. If you enjoy competitive shooters with depth, strong mechanics, and that unmistakable Halo feel, this one earns your time.
After a very rough start to its like Halo Infinite after many updates & about a year 1/2 has come good! A shame they let the hype of release slip to only have a great game almost 2 years in.

As somebody who has hardly scraped any of the previous Halo Multiplayer modes, I've enjoyed playing Infinate's multiplayer thanks to the nice-feeling gunplay. Despite not conforming to many of the traits I usually enjoy from FPS games (like Aim Down Sights and quick TTK), the game nails the feel of its approch to gunplay, and silenced any of my worries that it would feel outdated and try too hard to stick to the original games' feel.

Even though the Gameplay is near perfect in my eyes, the fact that the progression doesn't reward people based on contribution to team victory, and in fact rewards everybody the same no matter what, is kinda cringe.

In its current state it is a mechanically sound game to play that is a fundamentally half-baked and frustratingly rigid experience.
It's insane the amount of user control that has been removed from this game.
No map voting, tedious and conformist battle pass system, challenges dictate your progression as opposed to being a bonus on top of individual skill-based progression, cosmetics are scant and locked to cores, emblems are fixed and not actually customisable.

I have many many other grievances with the game that I can just live with but hope to change, but they are all just opinions derived from experiences past, primarily Reach & 4, which I constantly out of habit reference when I encounter something that just feels Wrong.
e.g. KBM vs Controller, "Tactical" Slayer, Map selection + design + balance (or lackthereof), very poor menu UX, player collision, melee reg, challenge progression bugs, 4v4 spawning.

I really want to like this game man but I can't in good faith say this is a great experience to pour hours into at this moment.

On a technical level, I do not believe this game is salvageable, which sucks because it should be great. The multiplayer gameplay, maps, modes, armour, weapons, and vehicles are all stellar. But the engine and networking held it back. The progression system was both exploitative and unrewarding. These things should be fixable... if the engine was written by long-term employees, not by a rotating series of contract workers. If the multiplayer wasn't owned by the monetization team. If there was any vision beyond "let's be like Fortnite but too late and not trying hard enough."

I don't know how the campaign ends. For me, it ended facing up against two bullet-sponge hunters with no ammo or grenades, after spending an hour playing through tediously uninteresting hallway fights. I walked into that room and realized that I could not win this fight, that I didn't want to re-play the fights up until there, and that I didn't care to play through any of the story after that.

I had a lot of fun for some of my time in this game, but that is significantly outweighed by the disappointments. I still wish I could play the version of this game that actually lives up to its gameplay.

You have to pay $10 just to get a color on your spartan. Any cool armor is locked behind a paywall or unavailable because you missed the window. They couldnt even get the one thing they care about right; the store. Recycled garbage. Playlists are garbage. Any original mode like Swat or Team Snipers has been ruined. The campaign was even lackluster because they threw away the entire story 4 and 5 was building. New armor cores are garbage. No cross core. You cant even customize your emblem from the default selections like every previous title before it. Battlepass is nothing but filler, being that every 5 or so levels is a challenge skip, a garbage emblem/background, or the SAME COATING spread out across 10 different tiers. (for example you cant just unlock a coating and use it for everything, you have to unlock it for your spartan, individual vehicles, individual guns, etc)

The way the game PLAYS is good. (combat, driving, movement) But literally anything and everything else was done so poorly its embarassing to call this a Halo game.

Halo: Infinite is really 2 games. The Campaign is absolute garbage - basically the same poor quality narrative and juvenile dialogue that was showcased in Halo 5.

Halo I, II, III, & Reach were all directly linked by a continued narrative. Halo 4 was separated by a longer gap but was still internally consistent with the previous games.

Halo V and VI are not; they are sequels to a handful of novels that no one read, and RTS games that no one played. They re-write entire swaths of existing narrative, and are so much lower in quality that the dialogue sounds like it was written by a grade-school student. Truly embarrassing. This game's campaign has functionally destroyed any interest that most people had in the narrative and I don't see a way to pull this franchise back. The damage is irreparable.

The online multiplayer portion of the game is "fine". As a sandbox it is well managed and largely free of game-breaking bugs or glitches. I give it high marks for being well optimized even on older hardware, and scaling well into high resolution and high FPS with better hardware.

The in game cosmetics are obscenely overpriced, and most are also gated behind paid battle passes.

tldr.text: Mixed (68%): players praise the co-op and multiplayer most.
The price and monetization draw the most complaints, while bugs and crashes come up often.

details.text: Recent reviews are about as positive as the overall score, and far fewer of them complain about the price.
Players who review after very little play are much less positive, at 48% positive against 75% for those with a few more hours.
